content:
Dear FreshCart Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at your Zagreb-Jarun store. I have completed butcher training and have worked in butchery and meat-counter roles since 2015, with hands-on experience in carcass breakdown, meat preparation, food hygiene and customer service.

In my current role as a butcher, I break down beef, pork and lamb, then bone, trim and portion the meat for the counter. I also prepare fresh sausages, rotate cold-room stock each morning using FIFO, and record cold-room and display-counter temperature checks twice daily. My HACCP training and daily hygiene routines support the careful handling and presentation of fresh meat.

I enjoy helping customers choose cuts and quantities and explaining how to prepare them. I serve around 120 customers on a Saturday and have trained two apprentices in safe knife handling and cleaning routines. FreshCart’s “Ask the counter” promise and its emphasis on knowledgeable, helpful service reflect the kind of customer-facing work I value.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my practical butchery experience and reliability could contribute to your meat-counter team. Thank you for considering my application.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise cover letter with a clear opening, relevant evidence, and a professional tone. It directly connects the candidate’s butcher training, carcass breakdown, sausage production, FIFO stock rotation, temperature checks, HACCP training, customer service, and apprentice training to the role. The quantified evidence—serving around 120 customers on a Saturday—is particularly effective. The company-specific reference to FreshCart’s “Ask the counter” promise also demonstrates genuine alignment. The letter is complete and appropriately brief for a short-letter application.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The plain-text structure is highly ATS-friendly: standard headings are unnecessary for a cover letter, there are no tables, columns, graphics, unusual symbols, or parsing barriers, and the document includes important terms such as butcher training, carcass breakdown, meat preparation, food hygiene, HACCP, customer service, fresh sausages, FIFO, and temperature checks. AI screening probability is high because the letter clearly connects relevant experience to the advertised duties and requirements. A minor improvement would be to state the formal qualification using the exact wording “completed Vocational Certificate: Butcher” and to use the job description’s phrase “cut, portion and package fresh meat” only for the duties the candidate actually supports; the candidate’s material supports cutting and portioning, but not supermarket self-service packaging.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The cover letter aligns very well with the two must-have requirements and the central duties of the role. It shows completed butcher training, more than two years of meat-counter experience, HACCP knowledge, cutting and portioning, customer advice, FIFO rotation, and temperature-recording routines. Its emphasis on knowledgeable customer service, hygiene, reliability, and busy Saturday trading matches FreshCart’s culture signals. The candidate does not have the nice-to-have forklift licence, which is a genuine qualification gap rather than a document defect. The candidate also has no supermarket, self-service packaging, tray-sealer, or labelling-scale experience; the letter appropriately avoids claiming these skills. The strongest transferable experience is already presented accurately.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT: In the opening paragraph, change “I have completed butcher training and have worked in butchery and meat-counter roles since 2015” to “I hold a completed Vocational Certificate in Butchery from Food Trades School Zagreb and have worked in butchery and meat-counter roles since 2015.” This makes the formal qualification and the job-ad wording more explicit for ATS screening.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT: In the second paragraph, change “I break down beef, pork and lamb, then bone, trim and portion the meat for the counter” to “I break down beef, pork and lamb carcasses, then bone, trim, cut and portion fresh meat for the service counter.” This incorporates the supported keywords “carcasses,” “cut,” “portion,” “fresh meat,” and “service counter” without claiming unsupported self-service packaging experience.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT: In the closing paragraph, replace “practical butchery experience and reliability” with “practical butchery experience, HACCP discipline and reliable customer-counter service.” This ties the closing more directly to FreshCart’s stated priorities while remaining supported by the document and original candidate information.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "reliability"

I hold a completed Vocational Certificate in Butchery from Food Trades School Zagreb and have worked in butchery and meat-counter roles since 2015, with hands-on experience in carcass breakdown, meat preparation, food hygiene and customer service.

In my current role as a butcher, I break down beef, pork and lamb carcasses, then bone, trim, cut and portion fresh meat for the service counter. I also prepare fresh sausages, rotate cold-room stock each morning using FIFO, and record cold-room and display-counter temperature checks twice daily. My HACCP training and daily hygiene routines support the careful handling and presentation of fresh meat.

I enjoy helping customers choose cuts and quantities and explaining how to prepare them. I serve around 120 customers on a Saturday and have trained two apprentices in safe knife handling and cleaning routines. FreshCart’s “Ask the counter” promise and its emphasis on knowledgeable, helpful service reflect the kind of customer-facing work I value.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my practical butchery experience, HACCP discipline and reliable customer-counter service could contribute to your meat-counter team. Thank you for considering my application.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, concise, professional, and well targeted to FreshCart’s butcher/meat-counter role. It establishes the completed butcher training, nine years of relevant experience, carcass breakdown, fresh sausage production, FIFO stock rotation, temperature checks, HACCP training, customer advice, and apprentice training. The quantified Saturday customer volume adds credibility, while the reference to FreshCart’s “Ask the counter” promise demonstrates genuine alignment with its customer-service culture. The letter is appropriately brief and avoids unsupported claims. It could be marginally stronger by addressing the job’s packaging/service-counter preparation duties with the candidate’s truthful paper-wrapping experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses highly relevant, parseable keywords including “Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant,” “butcher training,” “carcass breakdown,” “bone,” “trim,” “cut,” “portion,” “fresh sausages,” “FIFO,” “temperature checks,” “HACCP,” “customer service,” and “service counter.” Its conventional text layout, standard headings-free letter format, and absence of tables, graphics, columns, or unusual symbols support ATS parsing. AI screening probability is high because the claims are specific, quantified, and closely connected to the advertisement. The letter does not explicitly use the job-ad phrase “package fresh meat” or mention self-service shelves, but the candidate’s material confirms only paper wrapping and no tray-sealer or supermarket experience, so those terms should not be added as claimed experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is very strong for the stated must-have requirements and the core duties. The document supports cutting and portioning fresh meat, advising customers on cuts and preparation, FIFO rotation, and temperature/hygiene checks. It also reflects FreshCart’s emphasis on knowledgeable, helpful service, reliability, hygiene, and pride in good work. The candidate’s practical experience is stronger than the minimum requirement. The candidate material shows no forklift licence, so that nice-to-have is a genuine gap rather than a document defect. The material also indicates no supermarket, self-service packaging, tray-sealer, or labelling-scale experience; these are role-experience gaps, but the cover letter correctly avoids inventing them.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the second paragraph, after “cut and portion fresh meat for the service counter,” add a truthful sentence such as: “I also wrap prepared orders in paper and maintain a clean, safe presentation at the counter.” This gives the letter a closer match to FreshCart’s fresh-meat preparation and packaging duties without implying supermarket self-service, tray-sealer, or labelling-scale experience.
